cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy approximately 100,000 light-years in diameter

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: It contains 100–400 billion stars, gas, dust and dark matter

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: The structure includes a central bar and bulge, a flat disc with spiral arms, and a spherical halo of globular clusters

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: The Sun is located about 26,000 light-years from the galactic centre in the Orion Arm

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the galactic centre (~4 million solar masses)

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Milky Way
cards.back: Dark matter makes up most of the Milky Way's mass — visible matter is only a small fraction

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — the milky way?
cards.back: 1. For The Milky Way questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating The Milky Way, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. For extended response questions, plan your answer: identify AO1/AO2/AO3 requirements first
Describe the structure of the Milky Way and the Sun's position within it. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the milky way, including key astronomical concepts, observational data, and theoretical models relevant to AQA 8463, Edexcel 1AS0. AO2 (Application of Knowledge): Apply knowledge and understanding of the milky way to both familiar and unfamiliar astronomical contexts, using observational evidence and theoretical principles
